usage: 고속버스 + 타다, the default way to say you'll travel by it
the building you depart from; 강남, 센트럴시티 등이 유명
우등 = 3 wide seats per row, more legroom and pricier; worth knowing when booking
예매 is the standard word for booking transport tickets in advance, often on the 코버스 app
examples: 부산 갈 때 KTX보다 고속버스가 훨씬 싸요.
When going to Busan, the express bus is much cheaper than the KTX.
common cost trade-off residents weigh; 보다 compares the two
주말이라 고속버스 표가 다 매진됐어요.
It's the weekend, so the express bus tickets are all sold out.
매진되다 = to sell out; book early on holidays
우등으로 예매하면 자리가 넓어서 편해요.
If you book the premium one, the seats are wide so it's comfortable.
explains why people pay extra for 우등
nuance: 고속버스 runs city-to-city on expressways with few or no stops, so people contrast it with the KTX (faster, pricier) and 시외버스 (more stops, smaller towns). For 20-30s on a budget it's the go-to for trips like Seoul-Busan when you don't mind the longer ride.
mistakes: Confusing 고속버스 with 시외버스 — 고속버스 is nonstop expressway travel between major cities, while 시외버스 makes more stops and reaches smaller towns.
Saying 고속버스역 — buses use 터미널, not 역 (역 is for trains and subways).

usage: used for trips to smaller cities or towns a 고속버스 doesn't reach
often shares a building with the 고속버스 terminal but a separate ticket window
시간표 = schedule; departures can be sparse, so check it
완행 stops at many towns; the opposite is 직행 (direct)
examples: 그 동네는 KTX가 안 가서 시외버스를 타야 돼요.
The KTX doesn't go to that town, so you have to take the intercity bus.
typical reason to use 시외버스; 안 가다 = doesn't go there
시외버스는 정류장에 자주 서서 시간이 더 걸려요.
The intercity bus stops at stations often, so it takes more time.
서다 here = to stop; explains the trade-off vs 고속버스
시외버스 막차가 8시라 서둘러야 해요.
The last intercity bus is at 8, so we have to hurry.
막차 (last bus) is a key word; rural lines end early
nuance: 시외버스 covers shorter regional routes and makes stops, so it reaches places the 고속버스 skips. Residents traveling to a friend's hometown or a small coastal town often have no choice but 시외버스, and schedules thin out fast in the evening.
mistakes: Treating 시외버스 and 고속버스 as the same thing — they leave from different windows and serve different routes.
Assuming frequent departures — rural 시외버스 lines may run only a few times a day, so always check the 시간표.

usage: read aloud as '케이티엑스'; the standard high-speed rail in Korea
done on the 코레일톡 (Korail Talk) app or at the station
특실 = first class, roomier; 일반실 = standard
자유석 = no assigned seat, cheaper; sit in any open seat in the 자유석 cars, unlike 입석 (standing)
examples: 서울에서 부산까지 KTX로 두 시간 반 걸려요.
From Seoul to Busan it takes two and a half hours by KTX.
the classic speed selling point; KTX로 = by KTX
KTX 표가 비싸지만 빠르니까 자주 타요.
KTX tickets are expensive but since they're fast I take it often.
captures the typical price-vs-speed reasoning
주말에는 KTX 입석밖에 없을 때도 있어요.
On weekends there are sometimes only KTX standing tickets left.
입석 = standing ticket; reality of holiday travel
nuance: KTX is the fast, premium option people compare against 고속버스 and the cheaper 무궁화호/ITX trains. For a 20-30s resident it's the obvious pick when you value time over money, but holiday tickets vanish quickly, leaving only 자유석 or 입석.
mistakes: Reading KTX as English letters — Koreans say 케이티엑스, so pronounce each letter in Korean.
Booking on the wrong app — KTX is Korail, so use 코레일톡, not the SRT app (SRT is a separate high-speed operator).

usage: the small step-through motorbike, very common for delivery riders
the ones zipping around with food; 배달 = delivery
you need a 원동기 or 2종 소형 license depending on engine size
legally required; 헬멧 안 쓰면 단속 대상
examples: 배달원들이 스쿠터로 음식을 빨리 가져다줘요.
Delivery workers bring food quickly by scooter.
everyday city scene; 가져다주다 = bring (to someone)
스쿠터는 좁은 골목도 잘 다녀서 편해요.
Scooters get through narrow alleys well, so they're convenient.
explains why they're popular; 다니다 = to get around
비 올 때 스쿠터 타면 너무 위험해요.
Riding a scooter when it rains is really dangerous.
practical safety note residents make
nuance: 스쿠터 specifically means the small automatic step-through motorbike, the kind delivery riders use, whereas 오토바이 is the broader word for any motorcycle. For a city resident the word comes up constantly because of food delivery and because scooter-share apps exist.
mistakes: Using 스쿠터 for an electric kick-scooter — that's a 전동킥보드; 스쿠터 has a seat and an engine.
Assuming no license is needed — even small scooters require at least a 원동기 license.

usage: 운전하다 is the standard verb for driving any vehicle
the small cargo truck everyone uses for moving; read '일 톤 트럭'
the truck a moving company brings; 이사 = moving house
대 is the counter for vehicles, not 개
examples: 이사할 때 1톤 트럭을 빌렸어요.
I rented a one-ton truck when I moved.
very common DIY-move situation; 빌리다 = to rent/borrow
길에 트럭이 서 있어서 차가 막혀요.
A truck is parked on the road, so traffic is backed up.
서 있다 = to be parked/standing; 막히다 = to be jammed
과일 파는 트럭이 동네에 자주 와요.
A truck selling fruit often comes to the neighborhood.
the 트럭 행상 scene is common; 파는 modifies 트럭
nuance: 트럭 is everyday vocabulary because the 1톤 트럭 is the default vehicle for moving apartments and for the street vendors who sell fruit or vegetables from the back. Residents most often meet the word when arranging a move or dodging a double-parked one.
mistakes: Counting trucks with 개 — vehicles take the counter 대, so it's 트럭 한 대.
Pronouncing it like English 'truck' with a hard ending — in Korean it's two syllables, 트럭.

usage: 빌리다 = to rent/borrow; the standard verb here
done online before a trip, especially for 제주도
보험 = insurance; always ask about 자차 (collision) coverage
반납 = return; note the fuel and time rules
examples: 제주도에서는 렌터카가 없으면 다니기 힘들어요.
On Jeju Island it's hard to get around without a rental car.
the #1 렌터카 use case for residents; 다니다 = to get around
렌터카 빌릴 때 면허증하고 신용카드가 필요해요.
When you rent a car you need your license and a credit card.
practical requirement; 하고 links the two items
기름을 가득 채워서 반납해야 돼요.
You have to return it with a full tank.
common 만탱크 return rule; 가득 채우다 = to fill up
nuance: 렌터카 is the word residents reach for when planning a trip somewhere public transport is weak, above all 제주도, where everyone rents. Note it's a fixed loanword spelled 렌터카 (not 렌트카), and you'll always be asked about 보험 options at the counter.
mistakes: Spelling or saying it as 렌트카 — the standard form is 렌터카.
Forgetting you usually need a credit card in your own name plus a valid license (an international permit if your home license isn't accepted).

usage: Seoul's public bike-share; the name is friendly/cute
대여 = rental/checkout; done by app at a 대여소
반납 = return; you dock it at any station
정기권 = a pass (e.g. monthly); cheaper than per-ride
examples: 한강에서 따릉이 타면 진짜 시원해요.
Riding a Ttareungi by the Han River feels really refreshing.
the iconic 따릉이 activity; 시원하다 here = refreshing
지하철역까지 따릉이로 금방 가요.
I get to the subway station quickly by Ttareungi.
common last-mile use; 금방 = in no time
따릉이 앱으로 잠금을 풀어요.
You unlock the Ttareungi with the app.
잠금을 풀다 = to unlock; how the system works
nuance: 따릉이 is Seoul's public bike-share, so the word is specific to the capital (other cities have their own, like 타슈 in Daejeon). For a 20-30s Seoul resident it's a cheap last-mile option and a Han River weekend staple, rented and returned entirely through the app.
mistakes: Using 따릉이 for any bicycle — a personal bike is just 자전거; 따릉이 is the branded share system.
Assuming it exists nationwide — 따릉이 is Seoul-only; look for the local equivalent elsewhere.

usage: the standing share scooters from apps like 킥고잉, 씽씽
you need at least a 원동기 license to ride one legally
공유 = shared; the app-based ones parked on sidewalks
examples: 요즘 길에 전동킥보드가 아무 데나 세워져 있어요.
These days electric kick-scooters are parked all over the place.
common complaint; 아무 데나 = just anywhere
전동킥보드는 헬멧을 안 쓰면 벌금을 내요.
If you don't wear a helmet on a kick-scooter, you pay a fine.
real rule since 2021; 벌금 = fine
전동킥보드로 회사까지 십 분이면 가요.
I can get to work in ten minutes on a kick-scooter.
the convenience point; -이면 = if it's (just) ten minutes
nuance: 전동킥보드 is the standing electric scooter, almost always meaning the app-rented shared ones you see abandoned on sidewalks. Residents need the word both for the convenience and for the rules: a license and helmet are legally required, and crackdowns are real.
mistakes: Confusing it with 스쿠터 — 전동킥보드 is a standing electric scooter with no seat, not a motorbike.
Thinking it's rule-free — riding two people, no helmet, or with no license can all get you fined.

usage: small green local buses that fill gaps to subway stations
정류장 = bus stop; routes wind through neighborhoods
routes carry a district prefix plus a short number, like 종로11 or 강남07
환승 = transfer; you tap to transfer to the subway/regular bus
examples: 언덕 위 집까지 마을버스를 타고 가요.
I take the village bus up to my house on the hill.
classic use — hilly neighborhoods; 언덕 = hill
마을버스는 작아서 출근 시간에 사람이 꽉 차요.
The village bus is small, so it's packed during commute hours.
꽉 차다 = to be packed full
지하철에서 내려서 마을버스로 갈아타세요.
Get off the subway and transfer to the village bus.
common directions; 갈아타다 = to transfer
nuance: 마을버스 are the small local buses that connect residential pockets, especially hilly ones, to the nearest subway station or main bus route. A resident living off the main road relies on them daily, and they're short, frequent, and tightly looped through the neighborhood.
mistakes: Expecting it to travel far — 마을버스 only loops the local area to feed bigger lines, unlike a city or 광역버스.
Forgetting to tap for transfer — without tapping your card the 환승 discount to the subway won't apply.

usage: red express buses linking Seoul with nearby cities like 수원, 일산
they're seat-only; 입석 (standing) is restricted on these
노선 = route; long commuter runs into the metro center
color-coded red, vs blue/green city buses
examples: 분당에서 강남까지 광역버스로 출근해요.
I commute from Bundang to Gangnam by wide-area bus.
the prototypical 광역버스 commute; 출근하다 = to commute to work
광역버스는 자리에 앉아서 갈 수 있어서 좋아요.
The wide-area bus is nice because you can sit the whole way.
main appeal vs a packed subway
출근 시간에는 광역버스가 만석이라 한 대 보냈어요.
At rush hour the wide-area bus was full, so I let one pass.
만석 = full (all seats taken); 한 대 보내다 = let one go by
nuance: 광역버스 are the red long-distance commuter buses that connect Seoul with surrounding 경기도 cities, designed so suburban commuters can sit the whole ride. A 20-30s resident living outside Seoul but working in it will know these well, including the pain of a 만석 bus at rush hour.
mistakes: Mixing it up with 마을버스 — 광역버스 covers long city-to-city commutes, while 마을버스 only circles a neighborhood.
Expecting to stand — these are largely seat-only, so a full bus means waiting for the next one.

usage: the gondola up mountains or to coastal viewpoints
왕복 = round trip; the opposite is 편도 (one way)
표 = ticket; buy at the lower station
the lower station; -는 곳 = the place where you do it
examples: 남산 케이블카 타면 서울 야경이 정말 예뻐요.
If you ride the Namsan cable car, the Seoul night view is really pretty.
famous date spot; 야경 = night view
케이블카 왕복으로 끊는 게 더 싸요.
Buying a round-trip cable car ticket is cheaper.
표를 끊다 = to buy a ticket (idiom)
바람이 너무 세서 케이블카 운행을 멈췄어요.
The wind was too strong, so they stopped running the cable car.
운행을 멈추다 = to suspend operation; weather closures happen
nuance: 케이블카 is leisure-and-tourism vocabulary, the gondola you take up 남산, 통영, or 여수 for the view rather than for transport. Residents meet the word planning weekend trips and dates, and should know that strong wind can shut it down on the day.
mistakes: Calling a ground tram or funicular a 케이블카 — that's a 모노레일 or 트램; 케이블카 hangs from a cable.
Buying two 편도 tickets when a 왕복 ticket is cheaper for a there-and-back trip.

usage: the passenger/car ship to islands; also called 여객선
예매 = advance booking; island routes can fill up
차량 = vehicle; the kind you can drive your car onto
터미널 = terminal; the port building you board from
examples: 섬에 가려면 페리를 타야 돼요.
To get to the island you have to take a ferry.
core use case; -려면 = in order to
파도가 높아서 오늘 페리가 다 결항됐어요.
The waves are high, so all the ferries were canceled today.
결항되다 = (a ship/flight) to be canceled; common in bad weather
페리에 차를 싣고 제주도에 갔어요.
I loaded my car onto the ferry and went to Jeju.
싣다 = to load (cargo); the car-ferry option to Jeju
nuance: 페리 is the word for a passenger or car ship to Korea's islands; in formal notices you'll also see 여객선. A resident planning a trip to 제주도, 울릉도, or a small island needs it, and should expect 결항 (cancellations) whenever the sea is rough.
mistakes: Confusing 페리 with a sightseeing cruise — a tour boat is a 유람선; 페리 is point-to-point transport.
Not checking the weather — rough seas cause 결항, so an island ferry plan can fall through last minute.
